title: How a pull request gets merged
summary: The standard review workflow: who does what from open to merge, with the two decisions and the one wait. Explanatory: no questions.

blocks.title: Pull request review
blocks.trigger: a pull request is opened against main

lanes.label: Author
lanes.detail: Whoever opened the PR, human or agent.

lanes.label: CI
lanes.detail: The affected-checks workflow and the gates.

lanes.label: Reviewer
lanes.detail: A fresh-context reviewer; never the author's own model family.

lanes.label: Merger
lanes.detail: The owner, or the auto-merge bot once enabled.

steps.title: Open the PR with a plain-language impact line
steps.summary: Title, body, hyperlinked PR mentions, screenshots for UI.

steps.title: Run affected checks
steps.summary: Lint, gates, tests for the packages the diff touches.

steps.title: Green?
steps.summary: A red check blocks review; the author fixes first.

steps.title: Fix and push
steps.summary: Address the failure; CI re-runs on push.

steps.title: Review in fresh context
steps.summary: Code, architecture, comments, simplicity, anything else. One review with findings, each with one recommendation.
warnings: Reviews are comment-only. The reviewer never pushes fixes; the author or another process does.

steps.title: Approve or request changes?
steps.summary: Bikeshedding is declined; real issues and cheap clear nits are fixed.

steps.title: Respond to each finding
steps.summary: Fix, or decline with a reason, per finding. Push once.

steps.title: Wait for a second review when the change is risky
steps.summary: Two reviews before merge for anything that touches a gate or a release.

steps.title: Merge and pull the main checkout
steps.summary: Squash or merge per the repo rule; then the installed plugin is refreshed from main.
